subject: CAIQ onboarding: control mapping, evidence owners, and intake cadence
messages:
From: Alice Morales <alice.morales@clearwavehealth.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: secops@clearwavehealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CAIQ onboarding: initial scope and sample evidence ask

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our security team ran a light review of the CAIQ you shared and we have a few follow-ups before we can move to the artifact intake stage: 

- Can you confirm which Redwood deployments will be in-scope for ClearWave (hosted API only, or dedicated/private options)?
- We need a mapping table that ties each CAIQ control to an evidence artifact and an owner. A simple index works for now.
- For cryptographic key management: sample logs showing key rotation + KMS provider details (redacted values acceptable).
- Expected cadence for artifact delivery and point-of-contact for expedited requests.

Would you be available for a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow? If so, please share the intake template you plan to use.

Thanks,
Alice Morales
Senior InfoSec Manager
ClearWave Health

P.S. attaching our internal questionnaire snippets as separate mail to avoid overloading this thread.
From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
To: Alice Morales <alice.morales@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ onboarding: initial scope and sample evidence ask

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front: hosted API and Dedicated pools are in-scope for the ClearWave engagement; Private (on-prem) is out of scope unless you request it in writing.

Attaching our draft evidence index ("RI_evidence_index_v0.9.xlsx") and a scoped questionnaire worksheet that maps CAIQ control IDs to artifacts and owners. The index includes a column for delivery ETA and redaction notes.

Proposed intake cadence:
- Week 0: walk-through + scope sign-off
- Week 1–2: artifact harvest (owners supply artifacts)
- Week 3: ingest and QA, we surface gaps
- Week 4: closure meeting with attestation plan

For key rotation logs we can provide anonymized rotation entries and the KMS vendor (AWS KMS for Hosted/Dedicated). Kimberly (cc'd) will confirm the exact log format we can provide.

I can do a 30-min sync tomorrow 11:00–12:30 PT. Marcus — can you and Kimberly join to confirm owners and any nonstandard controls?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RI_evidence_index_v0.9.xlsx (spreadsheet), ClearWave_CAiq_Scope_Questions.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com, Alice Morales <alice.morales@clearwavehealth.com>, secops@clearwavehealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 12:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ onboarding: initial scope and sample evidence ask

Marissa / Alice —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from the security side: 
- Evidence ownership: We'll assign per-control stewards. Jordan will own runtime-telemetry controls (logging, replayability proofs). I'll own cryptography/KMS and identity controls. Marcus will be the escalation lead for any policy exceptions.
- KMS logs: attached sample file "auth-rotation-logs-sample.txt" is sanitized. We can supply more detailed CloudTrail excerpts via our secure intake link if you need them.
- Sensitive PHI/PHI-adjacent examples: Redwood never persists input data in plain logs for hosted customers by default; we will provide the retention and redaction policy excerpt with the index.

On the CAIQ mapping: please highlight any controls you consider "high-priority" for early delivery (we will surface owners for those first). Typical customers flag controls related to tenant isolation, telemetry, and key management.

Proposed attendees for tomorrow's sync (11:30 PT):
- Alice Morales — ClearWave InfoSec
- Marissa Cole — CS (intake lead)
- Marcus Lin — Security SL/Customer Escalations (owner)
- Kimberly Park — Head of Compliance
- Jordan Blake — Platform Security Engineer
- Neha Kapoor — Engagement Manager (notes and follow-up)

I'll upload the evidence index to the shared drive after the meeting and lock editing until owners are assigned.

Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
To: Alice Morales <alice.morales@clearwavehealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com, secops@clearwavehealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ onboarding: initial scope and sample evidence ask

Alice / team —

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. Confirming the 11:30 PT sync (calendar invite to follow). A few operational notes ahead of the call so we can be efficient: 

1) Prep ask for ClearWave: please flag the top-10 CAIQ control IDs you need first, and indicate if any controls will require tenant-level sampling versus platform-level artifacts. That will help us prioritize shipments.

2) Intake template: the attached RI_evidence_index_v0.9.xlsx is intentionally minimal — columns: control_id, short_description, artifact_filename, artifact_owner, delivery_eta, redaction_needed, notes. Please use it as the canonical intake for the engagement.

3) Secure exchange: for artifacts with sensitive content (logs with potential user identifiers) we will provision a temporary S3 share with encryption; expect a DocuSign-like access agreement. Link to provisioning ticket model in HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/CW-2026-045.

4) Escalation window: If ClearWave needs a faster turnaround on any control (SLA under 72 hours), mark it in the index and we will route to our expedited evidence lane (approval required by me).

I'll run the meeting and Kimberly/Jordan will triage owner assignment live. Neha will capture action items and upload the post-call artifact manifest.

See you at 11:30.

--
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Security Escalations
Redwood Inference
